Learning points

What this training run shows

Use the map with the measured results. The visual helps you inspect the model. The saved experiment files provide the evidence.

0.554

The token vector changed.

The bottleneck vector moved by an L2 distance of 0.554 from its recorded random start. Training changed a real model parameter.

0.698

Context changed local relationships.

After training, constraint is the closest displayed neighbor of bottleneck. The score uses cosine similarity in the full 64-dimensional space.

1,500

Validation loss gave an earlier warning.

Validation loss was lowest at step 1,500. It increased by step 3,000 while training loss continued to fall. This pattern is evidence of overfitting.

4,816

The corpus shaped the output.

The combined corpus contains 4,816 unique passages. Classroom sentences make up most passages. They also dominate unconditional generated text.

64D → 3D

The map is a view, not the full space.

PCA compresses the embeddings for display. Use the displayed neighbor scores and the saved checkpoint when you need the underlying measurement.

Optional: choose checkpoint.json from your results ZIP. Files stay on your device.
How this view stays faithful to the model

The map uses unnormalized token lookup vectors (weights.wte), not position embeddings, attention weights, or the context-dependent representations produced later in the network. Axes are principal components, not named concepts.

Similarity uses cosine in the original vector space, from −1 (opposite directions) through 0 to +1 (same direction). It is not a probability or proof of shared meaning. *The highlighted neighbors use this full-space similarity, so they need not be the nearest dots in the compressed 3D map.

Movement lines join the recorded endpoints. They do not show the actual training path or intermediate steps. Before/after comparisons here apply to one run, not independently trained models whose coordinates may differ.

Open checkpoint.json from this nanoGPT lab to inspect your own run, including its recorded initial table. Legacy checkpoints without an initial table disable the comparison. Supports up to 512 tokens and 64 dimensions. Only the selected token and its closest neighbors are labeled to keep the map readable; select any dot or use the token menu.

Evidence first. Interpretation second.
